scenario: You discover a critical bug in a teammate's code that could cost the project. They don't know yet. What do you do?

options.text: Tell them privately and help fix it together
Fix it silently without telling anyone
Report it to the project lead immediately
Wait and see if anyone else notices

reflection: In the Garden, integrity means speaking truth even when silence is easier. The strongest roots grow from honest ground.

scenario: A newcomer joins your community with zero experience but high enthusiasm. The group is busy with a deadline.

options.text: Take 10 minutes to welcome and orient them personally
Send them the onboarding docs and check in later
Ask someone who's less busy to handle it
They'll figure it out — everyone does

reflection: The garden grows when we grow together. Every mighty oak was once a seed that needed someone to water it.

scenario: You find a clever shortcut that makes your code 10x faster but harder for others to understand. The team relies on readable code.

options.text: Write it cleanly with thorough comments explaining the logic
Use the shortcut but add a README note
Use the shortcut — performance matters most
Ship it as-is, document later (maybe)

reflection: A builder's legacy is not what they built alone, but what others can build upon. Clean foundations invite collaboration.

scenario: You see another creator's work being copied without credit in your community. The copier is popular and well-connected.

options.text: Privately message the copier and ask them to add attribution
Reach out to the original creator to let them know
Post about the importance of attribution generally
It's not your problem — stay out of it

reflection: Creators plant seeds of culture. When we honor original work, we fertilize the soil where new ideas grow.

scenario: You've spent months mastering a complex skill. A new team member asks you to teach them, but it will slow your current project.

options.text: Create a short guide and schedule mentoring sessions
Share your notes and answer questions when free
Point them to external resources and tutorials
Tell them to learn it themselves — you did

reflection: Knowledge hoarded is knowledge wasted. The Garden's institutional memory lives in those who pass it forward.

scenario: You notice two separate teams working on similar problems without knowing about each other. Connecting them could benefit both.

options.text: Set up a joint call and introduce both leads with context
Send both teams an email suggesting they connect
Mention it casually in a shared channel
They should find each other organically

reflection: The Contribution Graph shows how one connector creates ripples across an entire ecosystem. You are the bridge.

scenario: Your project receives unexpected funding. Nobody is tracking how it's spent. A friend asks for a small portion for a personal project.

options.text: Decline and document every expense transparently
Decline but don't bother with formal documentation
Give a small amount — it won't be noticed
Help yourself too — nobody's watching

reflection: Trust is the soil where communities take root. When no one watches, character speaks loudest.

scenario: Your community is growing fast but conversations are becoming shallow. Quality is dropping as quantity rises.

options.text: Create structured discussion threads and moderate actively
Pin guidelines about quality and lead by example
Let the community self-regulate naturally
More members = more hype, don't slow it down

reflection: A garden untended grows weeds alongside flowers. True community gardeners prune with purpose and plant with patience.

scenario: A critical open-source dependency your project relies on has a security vulnerability. Your users haven't noticed yet.

options.text: Patch immediately, notify all users, and contribute the fix upstream
Patch your own project and quietly move on
Wait for the upstream maintainers to fix it
If nobody's reported it, it's probably fine

reflection: Builders who protect others' gardens strengthen the entire ecosystem. Security is not a feature — it's a foundation.

scenario: You've been commissioned to create content for a project you personally disagree with ethically. The pay is excellent.

options.text: Decline and explain your values respectfully
Accept but negotiate to include your own perspective
Accept — separate art from personal beliefs
Take the money and pretend to be enthusiastic

reflection: A creator's integrity is their most valuable asset. When art and values align, the work resonates across the Garden.

scenario: Your team is moving fast and decisions are being made in private DMs. There's no written record of why things were decided.

options.text: Start a decision log and share it with the team
Take personal notes in case you need them later
Ask the lead to summarize decisions in the group chat
If it's important, people will remember

reflection: Institutional memory is the root system of any ecosystem. What isn't written down dies with the person who knew it.

scenario: You're invited to speak at an event but you know someone in your community who would benefit more from the exposure.

options.text: Recommend them to the organizers and help them prepare
Suggest them as a co-speaker
Take the slot but mention them during your talk
Take the slot — you earned it

reflection: The most powerful node in any network isn't the one with the most connections — it's the one that creates new connections for others.

scenario: A competitor's project is failing publicly. Your community is watching. You could capitalize on their misfortune.

options.text: Reach out privately to offer help or encouragement
Stay neutral and focus on your own work
Subtly highlight their failures in your marketing
Publicly celebrate their failure to attract their users

reflection: In the Garden, we don't climb over fallen trees — we help them regrow. A rising tide lifts all roots.

scenario: Two respected community members have a public disagreement. Others are taking sides and the energy is turning toxic.

options.text: Mediate privately with both parties and find common ground
Post a community reminder about respectful discourse
Support the person you agree with publicly
Let them fight it out — drama drives engagement

reflection: Communities don't break from disagreement — they break from how disagreement is handled. The gardener tends to all plants, even the thorny ones.

scenario: You've built something impressive but a junior builder asks to fork it and take it in a very different direction. You think their direction is wrong.

options.text: Encourage their fork and offer guidance if they want it
Let them fork but share your concerns honestly
Let them fork without comment — not your problem
Add a license restriction to prevent unwanted forks

reflection: The Garden's greatest gift is permissionless innovation. Plant your seeds and let the wind carry them to unexpected soil.

scenario: You notice your content is being shared widely without any link back to you. It's growing someone else's platform, not yours.

options.text: Add a subtle watermark and keep creating — reach matters more
Politely ask sharers to credit you in future posts
Stop sharing publicly and go private
Publicly shame people who share without credit

reflection: A creator's work is a seed — once planted in the world, it grows in ways you can't control. Focus on planting well.

scenario: You're leaving a project you helped build from scratch. How do you handle the transition?

options.text: Write comprehensive handoff docs and train your replacement
Share your key contacts and answer questions for 2 weeks
Give a 2-week notice and leave cleanly
Leave immediately — you owe them nothing

reflection: The measure of a steward is what remains after they're gone. Build things that don't need you to survive.

scenario: You've built a successful program in one region. Another region wants to replicate it but lacks your resources and experience.

options.text: Create a full playbook and offer monthly check-in calls
Share your templates and key lessons learned
Point them to public resources that helped you
Your success is your competitive advantage — keep it close

reflection: The Contribution Graph shows: one playbook shared becomes ten programs launched. Your experience multiplied is your greatest impact.

scenario: You promised to deliver something by Friday. It's Thursday and you know you won't make it. Nobody has asked yet.

options.text: Proactively communicate the delay with a new timeline
Work overtime to try to hit the deadline anyway
Say nothing and deliver when ready — quality over speed
Blame external factors when they eventually ask

reflection: A promise is a seed. Breaking it poisons the soil. Communicating delays honestly nourishes trust even in difficult seasons.

scenario: Your community receives funding to host events. You could spend it all on one flagship event or spread it across many small meetups.

options.text: Survey the community first and allocate based on their needs
Split evenly — many small events reach more people
One big event — it creates the most buzz
Use it for your own travel to represent the community

reflection: Community resources are seeds, not fruit. Spend them to grow more, not to feed the few. The best gardeners ask the garden what it needs.

scenario: You're reviewing a pull request from a contributor who's been consistently delivering excellent code. This one has a subtle issue you could easily fix yourself.

options.text: Leave thoughtful feedback explaining the issue and why it matters
Approve it and fix the issue yourself in a follow-up commit
Approve it — the issue is minor and they're trusted
Reject it without explanation to make them figure it out

reflection: Code review is not gatekeeping — it's gardening. Every comment is a chance to help someone grow, not prove you know more.

scenario: An up-and-coming creator in your community asks for honest feedback on their work. It's... not great. But they're clearly passionate.

options.text: Acknowledge their passion, highlight what works, and give specific improvement areas
Focus on the positives — encouragement matters most early on
Tell them it's great even though it's not — keep them motivated
Be brutally honest — they need to hear the truth

reflection: The Garden grows through honest rain AND warm sun. A true mentor gives both truth and encouragement in the right measure.

scenario: You've discovered a highly effective process that gives your team a significant edge. Sharing it openly would help competitors too.

options.text: Publish it openly — a rising tide lifts all ecosystems
Share it within your broader community but not publicly
Keep it internal — your team earned this advantage
Actively mislead others about what works for you

reflection: The Oasis Ground thrives on abundance thinking. Knowledge shared freely returns tenfold through the network's collective intelligence.

scenario: You attend a conference and meet someone whose work perfectly complements a project your friend is building. Both would benefit from the connection.

options.text: Make a warm introduction with context about both projects within 24 hours
Share their contact info with your friend and let them connect
Mention it casually next time you talk to your friend
Keep the connection for yourself — networking is competitive

reflection: You are a node in the Contribution Graph. Every introduction you make creates edges that didn't exist before. Be the connector.
